Animated PowerPoint slide from a ggplot

Source: R/ggppt.R
ggppt.Rd

Puts a saved ggplot on a PowerPoint slide as a stack of editable vector shapes: one static base (axes, grid, legend, titles and the static layers) and one transparent shape per animation step, all at the same position. Native PowerPoint entrance animations are written for the steps, so in the slide show each step appears on click (or automatically).

Usage

ggppt(
  p,
  file = NULL,
  animate = NULL,
  scope = c("layers", "all", "all_but_theme"),
  title = NULL,
  effect = "appear",
  trigger = "click",
  duration = 0.5,
  doc = NULL,
  template = NULL,
  size = c("16:9", "4:3"),
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL,
  left = NULL,
  top = NULL,
  location = NULL,
  editable = TRUE,
  bg = "white",
  categorical = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

p

A saved ggplot object.

file

Path of the `.pptx` to write. If `doc` is given and `file` is `NULL`, nothing is written and the updated `doc` is returned.

animate

Layers at which a new step starts. Layers before the first entry are always shown; the last entry also reveals all later layers. `animate = c(3, 4, 5)` shows layers 1-2, then adds 3, then 4, then 5 and everything after it. `NULL` (default) reveals every layer on its own. A negative number removes a step again: `-3` makes the step that started at layer 3 disappear (with the given `effect` as exit animation in PowerPoint), e.g. `animate = c(3, 4, 5, -3)`. Entries play in the order given, and `effect`, `trigger` and `duration` count removals as steps.

scope

What the numbers in `animate` count: `"layers"` (default), `"all"` or `"all_but_theme"`. See [ggtex()] for details. With `"all"` and `"all_but_theme"` each step is a full redraw of the plot (on a `bg` background) that covers the previous one, because components such as titles or themes change the layout.

title

Slide title. `NULL` for no title.

effect

Entrance effect: `"appear"`, `"fade"`, `"wipe_left"`, `"wipe_right"`, `"wipe_up"` or `"wipe_down"`. One value, or one per step.

trigger

`"click"` (default), `"after"` (after the previous step) or `"with"` (with the previous step). One value, or one per step.

duration

Effect duration in seconds (ignored for `"appear"`).

doc

Optional existing `rpptx` object (from [officer::read_pptx()]) to add the slide to. Lets you build a whole deck with several plots.

template

Optional `.pptx` template whose theme and slide size are used for a new deck.

size

Slide size of a new deck when no `template` is given: `"16:9"` (default) or `"4:3"`. Ignored when `doc` or `template` is given.

width, height

Size of the plot on the slide in inches. Default: the free area below the title. Set the size here rather than by dragging in PowerPoint: dragging scales lines and points but not text, and resizing one step's shape misaligns it with the others. A full 16:9 slide is 13.33 x 7.5 inches.

left, top

Position of the plot's top-left corner in inches. Default: centred in the free area below the title.

location

Optional officer location for the plot (overrides `width`, `height`, `left`, `top`), e.g. `officer::ph_location(left = 1, top = 1.5, width = 8, height = 5)`. Defaults to the area below the title.

editable

If `TRUE`, the shapes and text of the plot can be edited in PowerPoint.

bg

Background of the full redraws used by `"all"` and `"all_but_theme"`. Should match the slide background.

categorical

If `TRUE`, every group within a step (each bar, box, colour group, line of a `colour =` mapping, ...) is revealed on its own, in group order. The step's `effect`, `trigger` and `duration` apply to each group, and a negative number removes all groups of that step at once. Only with `scope = "layers"`.

...

Further arguments for [rvg::dml()], e.g. `fonts`.

Value

If `file` is given, its path (invisibly); otherwise the updated `rpptx` object.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(ggplot2)
p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) +
  geom_point(colour = "grey70") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x) +
  geom_point(data = subset(mtcars, mpg > 30), colour = "red")
ggppt(p, "fuel.pptx", animate = c(2, 3), title = "Fuel use")
} # }
